entries.title: Finite offspring sampling reverses a genetic-epigenetic barrier ordering

fields.submit-name: Finite offspring sampling reverses a genetic-epigenetic barrier ordering
fields.submit-statement: Planidin et al. (2025) study a deterministic model of adaptive epigenetic divergence and identify finite-population extensions as future work. In an explicitly specified finite offspring-sampling extension, can pure environmental induction yield a larger neutral-marker fixation barrier than the matched genetic model? The narrow target here fixes one diploid adult per deme, two demes, migration m=1/4, selection s=1/2, recombination r=1/2, matched secondary-contact initialization and a single preselection migrant-marker pulse. It is a project-formulated special case of that research direction, not a conjecture stated verbatim by the authors.

fields.submit-posedBy: Project finite special case of Planidin et al., Adaptive epigenetic divergence can facilitate ecological speciation (2025), finite-population research direction.
fields.submit-resultNote: Finite sampling reverses the ordering in this matched model. Exact fixation probabilities are p_gen=323808055/4466354606 and p_epi=1/14. With RI=1-p/(1/8), RI_gen=937945083/2233177303 and RI_epi=3/7. Kernel-checked harmonic certificates identify the actual limits with error <=(99/100)^n; this is stronger than a numerical simulation. The matched deterministic genetic barrier exceeds 3/7 from generation four onward. This compares a finite-model limit with a deterministic finite-generation sequence, not an unproved ordering of both limits. The contribution is the exact comparison in the declared offspring-sampling model. Finite epigenetic models, normalized fixation and timing effects have prior literature. The phased-to-count reduction has rational checks and written review; Lean starts from the 81-state count model. No universal population-size law, observed species formation or full source-question closure is claimed.

entries.title: Identical genome-copy transmission histories with opposite organism-level IAP

fields.submit-name: Identical genome-copy transmission histories with opposite organism-level IAP
fields.submit-statement: In Alexander's specieslike-cluster framework, does a complete realized genome-copy transmission graph, together with any bounded prefix of organism ownership, determine the whole-population identical-ancestor property (IAP)? Consider the explicit class with four diploid organisms per generation, two distinct parents and two children per nonfounder/organism, witnessed parent-child edges and real generation birthdates. This inverse-observation question is a project-formulated follow-up; Alexander's source defines IAP and specieslike clusters but does not state this exact constrained question. Here IAP means that each organism has either finitely many descendants or finitely many non-descendants within the population.

fields.submit-posedBy: Project follow-up to S. A. Alexander, Specieslike clusters based on identical ancestor points (2026); the constrained inverse-observation question is formulated in this project.
fields.submit-resultNote: No: even complete realized copy-transmission data can miss decisive organism structure. For any finite N, two ownership schedules agree through N on one fixed eight-lane genomic history. Both pedigrees retain four diploid organisms per generation, two distinct parents per nonfounder, two children per organism, connectivity, real birthdates and exactly witnessed edges. One whole population satisfies IAP and is maximal specieslike; the other fails IAP after a permanent split. Thus no exact IAP decoder exists for this observation on the constructed family. This strengthens the example beyond an unconstrained missing-data argument. Finite truncations map to the Wong gARG structure, but edge preservation does not imply ancestry path lifting. This is deterministic ambiguity, not equal genotype likelihoods, positive probability of the infinite schedules or species classification. Prior pedigree ambiguity is credited; novelty concerns the precise conjunction, subject to external review.

fields.submit-posedBy: Project observation-recovery follow-up to the constrained diploid IAP construction (2026), using Alexander's specieslike-cluster framework.
fields.submit-resultNote: Within the mixing/delayed-split family, the complete co-ownership record determines IAP exactly when sampled odd generations are unbounded. Even observing the full ownership assignment at every even generation fails. The result separates informative timing from sheer observation volume. A positive query certifies splitting in this family; finitely many negative answers permit a later split. If a prior even bound B>=2 guarantees that any split occurs by B, a sampling set identifies IAP exactly when it contains an odd generation after B; one query at B+1 suffices. The infinite-record decoder is not a uniformly terminating algorithm. The sharp mask criterion is a model-specific deduction; pedigree ambiguity and finite/infinite monitoring distinctions have prior literature. Neither the observations nor this theorem establish the switch bound or biological applicability.

entries.title: Exact sampled-family recovery from independent binary inheritance blocks

fields.submit-name: Exact sampled-family recovery from independent binary inheritance blocks
fields.submit-statement: In a one-generation specialization motivated by Kim, Mossel, Ramnarayan and Turner's pedigree-reconstruction work, children belong to disjoint parental pairs, parental symbols at each block are all distinct, and every child copies either parent independently and fairly across children and blocks. Join sampled children when they share a symbol at any of B>=1 observed blocks, then take connected components. What is the exact probability that this observed graph recovers all sampled families, and is independence essential to the gain from additional blocks?

fields.submit-posedBy: Project one-generation follow-up to Kim, Mossel, Ramnarayan and Turner, Efficient Reconstruction of Stochastic Pedigrees (arXiv:2005.03810).
fields.submit-resultNote: The exact success probability is $\prod_i[1-(2^{m_i-1}-1)2^{-B(m_i-1)}]$. The proof connects actual observed-symbol components to a complete count of failure configurations: a family disconnects exactly when its inheritance vectors occupy one complementary pair, both present. For three siblings and two blocks, success is 13/16, versus 7/16 for the restricted all-three-sharing rule. Extra blocks cannot spoil recovery, but their probability benefit needs independence: repeating each child's choice across blocks preserves every block\'s fair joint marginal while three-sibling success stays 1/4. This is an exact finite-sample guarantee with a dependence counterexample. It assumes distinct parental symbols, disjoint parental pairs, fair independent copying and exact observations. It does not prove full REC-GEN, statistical optimality, a Wong-law coupling or infinite specieslike recovery. Priority remains unestablished.

entries.title: Current player membership does not determine a predecessor-restoring split

fields.submit-name: Current player membership does not determine a predecessor-restoring split
fields.submit-shortName: Merge history is needed for splitting
fields.submit-statement: Abramsky et al., Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems, section 6.4.3, ask how to model games whose actions merge or split the decision makers. For the precise predecessor-restoring operation motivated by the IPDm implementation, is the unordered partition of persistent sites into current players sufficient to determine the result of every admissible split of the same designated composite? This is one structural subproblem formulated by the project, not the complete changing-player game question.

fields.submit-resultNote: No. Two legal histories, merge(0,1) then merge({0,1},2), and merge(1,2) then merge(0,{1,2}), have the same unordered current partition {{0,1,2},{3}}. Splitting that same composite into its immediate predecessors yields different partitions. Lean proves legal histories, admissible splits, the fixed designated group and spectator, and no exact deterministic partition-only update even on admissible states. This identifies a concrete missing-state defect in the source-motivated operator model. A separate pinned IPDm operator test reproduces the collision with declared mocks. The quotient principle is established mathematics; no broad novelty is claimed. Full program refinement, stochastic reachability, controllers, payoffs and equilibrium theory remain open. The result is a structural partial advance, not closure of the authors' changing-player question.
